I've been playing Tower Defense for years, here are some of the titles I keep returning to over and over:

  • Gem Tower Defense (Flash)

This goes on the top of almost all my Tower Defense lists. My favorite thing about this game is the way that randomness is involved in your building design.

The basic game flow is as follows: Prospect 5 squares, producing 5 random towers on those squares. Choose one tower to keep, the rest turn into walls. Combine towers to make more powerful ones. Creep waves come after finalizing your tower choice.

This doesn't sound like much, but it's absolutely beautiful the way that placement and randomness interact. You want to put walls in non-ideal tower locations, but what if you randomly find an excellent tower in a poor location? Or the other way around - since you can delete walls, are you going to place that mediocre tower in a prime spot or keep repicking until you get your ideal choice?

The game does have some issues. Most notably is a memory overflow related to projectiles, which makes the game prone to crashing when you play Survival mode up into the high levels. There's also very little you can do while the creep wave is coming, so in later levels as you fill a maze with stuns and slows the game starts to become "Pick towers, then come back in 15min to see if you survived the wave."

  • Antbuster (Flash)

Antbuster is a fun TD game with a faster pace than Gem TD, and it features a unique creep-movement algorithm. The creeps have a more-or-less open field to move through, but they follow the previous paths of other creeps like ants following pheromone trails. This means that you can use "scary" towers like fire to keep them away from areas, or use ice towers to slow them and leave lots of scent in that area. This helps create a "kill zone" for the creeps but ultimately Antbuster is fun because it takes one of the key elements of TD - the maze - out of the player's hands.

  • Integrated Defense (Flash)

This game adds a power supply mechanic to the standard tower defense. Now you don't just place towers, you have to power them as well! Managing the power grid is fun and gives you a dynamic job to perform as the creeps run through. There are also many maps and clever tower designs that make the game feel interesting, unfortunately it also suffers from the projectile memory bloat that Gem TD has.

  • Snow Virus TD (Flash)

Towers upgrade in a colligative way, so you get to mix-n-match properties between Fast Fire, Area Damage, Range and Damage. There's also an elemental effect system that you can switch at will, plus some nice clean graphics and a wave-queue system. My big complaint is the lack of a Survival mode.

  • PX57 (Apple)

Fun because I helped make it! Arcade style and awesome all around. Unity environment. Creeps will follow pathing algorithms similiar to the Antbuster one, except they follow a "death avoidance" system, causing them to avoid paths upon which many creeps have already died.

There's also a procedurally generated map and a power delivery system that makes taking territory a big part of the fun. Where's the best place to put that power station? It's different every time.

  • Iron Brigade (Steam)

Fun because it's a 3rd person shooter with tower defense elements. You get to be a walking tower! Done by Double Fine Studios and definitely one of their crowning gems in my opinion. Great survival missions.
Thanks! Also, are there any tower defense games where every creep always reaches its destination and you have to do as much damage as possible?

**Daily Devotional**

**April 21**

*21 For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain. 22 But if I live in the flesh, this is the fruit of my labour: yet what I shall choose I wot not. 23 For I am in a strait betwixt two, having a desire to depart, and to be with Christ; which is far better: (Philippians 1:21-23 KJV)*

These verses show why Paul was such a dedicated Apostle, as he was dead to himself and for him to live was Christ living through him. He actually looked forward to his death so that he might be with Christ, which he considered to be much better. All Christians should feel this way, as it is a fact (Romans 8:18). He wrote these verses while he was in a Roman prison, facing possible death. That is why he says that if he lives in the flesh, his lot would be to suffer and be in prison, but he chooses what the Lord would have him do, and not what he would prefer to do.

Those who fear death are living in unnecessary bondage (Hebrews 2:15). If the Christian would think on Heaven, and the things that God has prepared for His children, we would know that we can not lose for winning. If we live, we live for Christ, and to do His calling in this world, but if we die, we get to go to be with Him, which is even better (John 14:2-3). We should continually praise God for all the blessings He has given us, that we can have eternal life now (John 17:3), not just when we get to Heaven. If you truly have a strong, knowing, kind of faith, you will not have any fear of death. Thank you Lord!

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
